# Review

## Duration

$$D = \sum_{t} t \cdot \frac{CF_t / (1+y)^t}{P}$$

The present-value-weighted average time to receipt, in years.

For a zero-coupon bond, $D$ equals maturity. For a coupon bond, $D$ is less than
maturity.

## Modified duration and the price approximation

$$D^* = \frac{D}{1+y}, \qquad \frac{\Delta P}{P} \approx -D^* \times \Delta y$$

A bond with $D = 7$ and $y = 4\%$ has $D^* = 6.73$. A 100 basis point rise in
yields gives

$$\frac{\Delta P}{P} \approx -6.73 \times 0.01 = -6.73\%$$

# Immunization

## Definition

A portfolio of bonds is immunized against a liability when two conditions hold
at the same time:

::: {.cards .cards-2}
::: {.card}
[Present value]{.card-title}

$$PV_{\text{assets}} = PV_{\text{liability}}$$
:::

::: {.card .card-blue}
[Duration]{.card-title}

$$D_{\text{assets}} = D_{\text{liability}}$$
:::
:::

Portfolio duration is the value-weighted average of the durations of the
holdings.

## The liability {.plain-title}

| | |
|---|---|
| Amount due | $1,000,000 |
| Due in | 7 years |
| Yield curve | flat at 4% |
| Present value | $759,918 |
| Duration | 7.00 years |

$$PV = \frac{1{,}000{,}000}{1.04^{7}} = 759{,}918$$

## Two bonds are available

| Bond | Maturity | Coupon | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 3 years | zero | 3.00 |
| B | 12 years | zero | 12.00 |

## Solving for the weights

Let $w$ be the fraction in bond A:

$$3w + 12(1-w) = 7$$

$$w = \frac{12 - 7}{12 - 3} = \frac{5}{9} = 0.5556$$

## The immunized portfolio {.plain-title}

| Bond | Weight | Amount invested | Face value at maturity |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 55.56% | $422,177 | $474,891 |
| B | 44.44% | $337,741 | $540,735 |
| Total | 100% | $759,918 | |

Present value matches the liability. Duration is
$0.5556 \times 3 + 0.4444 \times 12 = 7.00$.

# Shocks

## Parallel shift: yields rise 100 bp {.plain-title}

| | Value at 4% | Value at 5% |
|---|---|---|
| Bond A | $422,177 | $410,229 |
| Bond B | $337,741 | $301,101 |
| Assets | $759,918 | $711,330 |
| Liability | $759,918 | $710,681 |
| Surplus | $0 | $649 |

## Parallel shift: yields rise 400 bp {.plain-title}

| | Value at 4% | Value at 8% |
|---|---|---|
| Bond A | $422,177 | $376,984 |
| Bond B | $337,741 | $214,733 |
| Assets | $759,918 | $591,717 |
| Liability | $759,918 | $583,490 |
| Surplus | $0 | $8,227 |

## Non-parallel shift {.plain-title}

| | Rate | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Bond A (3 yr) | 4.50% | $416,146 |
| Bond B (12 yr) | 5.50% | $284,416 |
| Assets | | $700,562 |
| Liability (7 yr) | 5.00% | $710,681 |
| Surplus | | −$10,119 |

## What the two conditions do and do not deliver

::: {.cards .cards-3}
::: {.card}
[Holds]{.card-title}

Small parallel shifts, immediately after the match is struck.
:::

::: {.card .card-blue}
[Surplus]{.card-title}

Large parallel shifts, when asset convexity exceeds the liability's.
:::

::: {.card}
[Deficit]{.card-title}

Non-parallel shifts, and the passage of time, since durations drift apart.
:::
:::

Rebalancing is required as time passes and as rates move.

## Lab — build and break one {.band-bottom}

A liability of $2,500,000 due in 9 years. Flat curve at 3.8%. Available: a
4-year zero and a 15-year zero.

::: {.steps}
1. Build the immunized portfolio in the Unit 2 workbook
2. Revalue assets and liability at +100 bp and at +300 bp, parallel
3. Revalue again with short rates +25 bp and long rates +200 bp
:::

::: {.note}
Post the surplus or deficit under each of the three scenarios.
:::
